title: GAMMALN from 3 to 8 is a stored recurrence, and GAMMALN(3) is one unit above ln 2
statement: With RN(v) meaning v rounded to 64 bits on the x87 unit and then stored to binary64, write x = n + y with n the integer part. For 3 < x < 8, Excel forms z = (y+2)(y+3)...(y+n-1) from the left with every product RN, and GAMMALN(x) is RN(RN(ln z) + GAMMALN(2+y)). So answers on this range carry the rounding of a value on [2,3]. x = 3 itself belongs to the band on [2,3], not to this route, and returns 0x3fe62e42fefa39f0, one unit above the stored ln 2, although GAMMALN(3) is exactly ln 2.
basis: 6,000 of 6,000 fractions at each n from 3 to 7, 30,000 answers, from Excel's own GAMMALN(2+y) (build 20527). The descending product fits 5,430 to 5,527 of 6,000. Replayed for this note in exact rational arithmetic with a correctly rounded logarithm on 300 of those fractions: 300 of 300 at n = 3 to 6, and 299 of 300 at n = 7. Recorded rows match GAMMALN 2,106 of 4,538 and GAMMALN.PRECISE 10,627 of 14,278, with stand-ins for the bands below 3.
inferred: That GAMMALN.PRECISE takes the same route is inferred: the 30,000 answers are GAMMALN, and the two functions agree at every shared recorded input tried, including 3.
